::: {#def-loyalty .theorem}
## Loyalty

A component function $g_{ti}$ is loyal to graph $\mathscr{G}$ if for all $\mathbf{X}_t,\mathbf{X}'_t \in \{0,1\}^n$

$$
\mathbf{X}_{t\mathcal{N}_i} = \mathbf{X}'_{t\mathcal{N}_i} \implies g_{ti}(\mathbf{X}_t) = g_{ti}( \mathbf{X}'_t).
$$

A structural equation is loyal to graph $\mathscr{G}$ if it is separable and all its component functions are loyal to $\mathscr{G}$. Loyalty is implied by [positional invariance](#def-positional-invariance), taking $j=i$ and $\mathbf M = \mathbf I$.
:::
